title: Ring-only algebraic inverse-image presentation
statement: Let $(C,J),(D,K)$ be sites and $L:\operatorname{Sh}(J,\mathrm{Set})\to\operatorname{Sh}(K,\mathrm{Set})$. For ring sheaves $R,S$, a ring inverse-image presentation is an isomorphism $e:L|R|\cong |S|$ preserving addition, multiplication, zero and one on arbitrary generalized sections. Precisely, for every test sheaf $T$, source arrows $a,b,t:T\to |R|$ satisfying $t=a+b$ or $t=ab$ sectionwise, the arrows $eL(a),eL(b),eL(t)$ satisfy the same equation sectionwise on the target site. Every identically zero or one arrow remains so. This is exactly the ring-only portion of [def-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image]; it has no module functor or module operation.
